a: The era also produced genuine cast-iron pagodas, among them the Iron Pagoda of Yuquan Temple (Jade Springs Temple) in Dangyang, Hubei Province. Erected in 1061, it contains 53,848 kg (118,715 lb) of cast iron and rises 21.28 m (69.8 ft) high. Modeled on the wooden, stone, and brick pagodas of its day, it has sloping eaves and an octagonal base. Another iron pagoda, built in 1105 in Jining, Shandong, was cast layer by layer in octagonal sections and reached a height of 78 feet. A number of such cast-iron pagodas still survive in China today.

a: A great deal of Sholay was filmed in the rocky landscape around Ramanagara, a town near Bangalore in Karnataka. To reach the sets more easily, the filmmakers had to construct a road linking the Bangalore highway to Ramanagara. Art director Ram Yedekar erected an entire township on the location. A prison set was also built outdoors near Rajkamal Studio in Mumbai so that its natural lighting would match that of the on-location shoots. For a time, one section of Ramanagara was known as "Sippy Nagar" in honor of the film's director. As of 2010, tourists passing through Ramanagara were still offered a visit to the "Sholay rocks," where much of the film was shot.

a: A gold dollar had been put forward on several occasions during the 1830s and 1840s, yet it was not adopted at first. Congress was eventually spurred to act by the larger supply of bullion brought about by the California gold rush, and in 1849 it authorized a gold dollar. In its early years, silver coins were being hoarded or shipped abroad, so the gold dollar quickly found a useful role in commerce. Silver returned to circulation after Congress, in 1853, mandated that newly minted silver coins be made lighter, and the gold dollar grew scarce in everyday trade even before federal coins disappeared from circulation amid the economic upheaval of the American Civil War.
h: A gold dollar had been proposed several times in the 1830s and 1840s , but was not initially adopted . Congress was finally galvanized into action by the increased supply of bullion caused by the California gold rush , and in 1849 authorized a gold dollar . In its early years , silver coins were being hoarded or exported , and the gold dollar found a ready place in commerce . Silver again circulated after Congress in 1853 required that new coins of that metal be made lighter , and the gold dollar became a rarity in commerce even before federal coins vanished from circulation because of the economic disruption caused by the American Civil War .

a: Ever since the Spanish Armament of 1790, the Royal Navy had remained at sea in a state of readiness for more than three years. Under First Lord of the Admiralty Charles Middleton, the Navy's dockyards were all fully equipped and prepared for war. This stood in sharp contrast to the failures of the American Revolutionary War a decade earlier, when an unprepared Royal Navy had taken too long to reach full strength and was therefore unable to back the North American campaign — which ended in defeat at the Battle of Yorktown for want of supplies. With British dockyards now steadily producing cannon, shot, sails, provisions and other vital equipment, the sole remaining difficulty was manning the several hundred ships on the Navy's list.
h: Since the Spanish Armament of 1790 , the Royal Navy had been at sea in a state of readiness for over three years . The Navy 's dockyards under First Lord of the Admiralty Charles Middleton were all fully fitted and prepared for conflict . This was quite unlike the disasters of the American Revolutionary War ten years earlier , when an ill @-@ prepared Royal Navy had taken too long to reach full effectiveness and was consequently unable to support the North American campaign — which ended in defeat at the Battle of Yorktown due to lack of supplies . With British dockyards now readily turning out cannon , shot , sails , provisions and other essential equipment , the only remaining problem was that of manning the several hundred ships on the Navy list .
